advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Handle session-less claim edges in attempts_per_ticket so multiple `open->in_progress` events without a `session` key are not collapsed into one attempt.
evidence: src/rebar/metrics/event_metrics.py:185: `sessions.add(data.get("session"))`
src/rebar/_commands/txn.py:70-76 `_stamp_session` adds `session` only `if value:` — a session-less `open->in_progress` transition omits the key entirely
txn.py:273 comment: "Absent -> key omitted -> byte-identical" — confirms `session` is optional on the claim edge
ABSENCE: no guard distinguishes a present `session=None` from a genuinely distinct session-less claim; both map to the single set element `None`
advisory.finding: attempts_per_ticket counts distinct `data.session` values, but the `session` key is present-only on claim STATUS events (`_stamp_session` omits it when no session provenance resolves). Multiple distinct claim attempts that all lack a session key collapse to a single `None` element in the set, so N session-less re-claims count as 1 attempt instead of N — undercounting the core metric.
advisory.suggested_fix: Count distinct sessions but treat a missing `session` key as a distinct attempt (e.g. key each session-less edge by its event uuid/timestamp rather than adding a shared `None`).

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Guard event-file parsing (JSONDecodeError/OSError) so one corrupt or partial event file skips that file rather than aborting the whole metric.
evidence: src/rebar/metrics/event_metrics.py:92-96 `_load` opens and `json.load`s with no exception handling
src/rebar/metrics/event_metrics.py:181 `event = _load(path)` inside the scan loop, uncaught
codebase norm: graph/_status.py:47 and many graph/*.py sites wrap reduce_ticket in `except Exception` and skip the ticket
ABSENCE: no handling for a mid-write/truncated event file, which is a real state during concurrent writes
advisory.finding: _load performs an unguarded `json.load` with no try/except, and the derivation loops call it on every matched `*-STATUS.json`/`*.retired`/reduce path with no error handling. A single corrupt, partially-written, or foreign file ending in `-STATUS.json` raises (json.JSONDecodeError/OSError) and aborts the entire metric computation, unlike the rest of the codebase which wraps reduce_ticket/scan calls in try/except and skips unreducible entries.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Make rework_within_days present-detection range-aware for non-STATUS events (or fix the docstring) so a populated in-range store never reports Unavailable.
evidence: src/rebar/metrics/event_metrics.py:222: `if ticket_present or (_has_any_event(ticket_dir) and lo is None and hi is None):`
src/rebar/metrics/event_metrics.py:218: `ticket_present = True` is set only inside the STATUS-file loop
src/rebar/metrics/event_metrics.py:220-221 docstring: "STATUS events dominate but a ticket may exist via other event types too"
Scenario: a ticket created + commented within the range but never STATUS-transitioned in range yields present=False -> None despite existing in range
advisory.finding: rework_within_days present-detection contradicts its own docstring. The docstring says "a ticket may exist via other event types too", but when a range is supplied the fallback `_has_any_event(...) and lo is None and hi is None` is disabled, and `ticket_present` is only set from in-range STATUS events. A store where every in-range ticket has non-STATUS events but no in-range STATUS event returns None (Unavailable) instead of a measured 0.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add behavioral tests for reopen_recovery (reopen-edge count) and first_pass_rate (None-on-empty and the single/total fraction).
evidence: reopen_recovery defined: `def reopen_recovery(` and first_pass_rate: `def first_pass_rate(...) -> float | None` with branch `if not attempts: return None` / `single / len(attempts)`
register() appends specs for both: `_spec("reopen_recovery", reopen_recovery)` and `_spec("first_pass_rate", first_pass_rate)`

ABSENCE: neither `reopen_recovery` nor `first_pass_rate` is imported or asserted in tests/unit/metrics/test_event_metrics.py or tests/unit/metrics/test_event_metrics_heldout.py (imports are only `attempts_per_ticket, revert_recovery, rework_within_days`).
advisory.finding: Two of the five registered derivations — reopen_recovery and first_pass_rate — have no direct tests. reopen_recovery's reopen-edge detection and first_pass_rate's None-on-empty / single-count fraction arithmetic are entirely unexercised, so a regression in either (e.g. counting the wrong edge, or a division/None-branch error) would not be caught.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test that invokes a registered spec's compute (via a context object / evaluate) to verify repo_root/since/until wiring, the n=7 binding, and the ctx-None guard.
evidence: Adapter under test: `def compute(ctx): if ctx is None: return None; return fn(_ctx_repo_root(ctx), n, _ctx_since(ctx), _ctx_until(ctx))`
Only registry test asserts metadata: `assert is_authoritative(s.source) is True` and `agent_ids ... assert agent_ids` — never calls `s.compute(ctx)`.
ABSENCE: no test builds a context object and calls a registered spec's compute (or evaluate(spec, ctx)) to verify the derivation is reached with correct args and the n=7 binding is applied.
advisory.finding: The registry context-adapter (`_spec`/`compute`) — the stated integration purpose of the change — is never invoked by any test. The registration test asserts only `source`/`lens` metadata, so the adapter's argument wiring (pulling repo_root/since/until off ctx), the `n=7` binding for rework_within_7_days, and the `ctx is None -> None` guard are all regression-blind.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a range-boundary test that confirms an event just outside [since, until) is excluded and one just inside is included, exercising both the date-only and datetime `_bounds` branches.
evidence: Untested branch in `_bounds`: `if "T" not in until and ":" not in until: hi = _to_ns(dt + timedelta(days=1)) else: hi = _to_ns(dt) + 1`
Only range test window is wide and non-boundary: `rework_within_days(str(tmp_path), 7, since="2026-01-01", until="2026-12-31")` — every crafted event (2026-02-*) sits well inside it.
ABSENCE: no test places an event just before `since` or just at/after `until` to confirm it is excluded, nor exercises the datetime-bound (with 'T') inclusive-microsecond branch.
advisory.finding: The since/until range filtering is not exercised at its inclusion/exclusion boundary for any derivation. The only range test uses a full-year window that never trips the boundary, so the non-trivial date-only vs datetime `_bounds` branch (inclusive vs exclusive upper) and the `_in_range` cutoff are regression-blind.
